chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yahya al-Taweel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not make the tongue to extend and the hand to restrain, but He made both of them to extend together and restrain together.

key_terms.الْيَدِ: The hand, representing action or deed
key_terms.بَسْطَ: To extend, loosen, or be loose (in the context of speech or action)
key_terms.كَفَّ: To restrain, hold back, or be tight

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between speech and action in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the intrinsic unity of human faculties, teaching that eloquence and restraint are not isolated traits but co-regulated aspects of one's character. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on *mizan* (balance), where internal coherence between word and deed serves as a primary indicator of spiritual integrity and moral consistency.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Yahya Al Taweel, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has not Made the tongue to extend and the hand to restrain, but He<sup>azwj</sup> Made both of them to extend together, and restrain together (naturally)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Yahya af-Tawif who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah, the most Majestic, the most Glorious, has not made the tongue to extend and the hands to withhold but that He has made them to extend and withhold together.”
